## Design note

A real race car let loose in the city. On slick-like rubber, with a wing the size of a door and a sequential box that bangs through gears, it corners and brakes like nothing on the street — once it is up to speed. Below 80 km/h the aero does nothing and the stiff suspension skips over kerbs and manhole covers; the steering lock is poor and the tall first gear hates junction starts. Loud, low, unmissable.

## How this car breaks

Production-derived steel shell with a welded multi-point roll cage tying the pillars, sills and strut towers together: the cabin survives hits that write off the road supercars. Everything outside it is lightweight carbon and fibreglass — splitter, wings, doors and bumpers shatter or fly off on contact, and the front crash structure is short. Low ride height means kerb strikes damage the floor.

## Sources (type)

- series homologation sheets for 2010s front-engine GT endurance cars (minimum weight, restrictors, dimensions)
- team-published dyno and aero balance figures for restricted 5.5 L GT V8s
- on-board telemetry figures for the class (braking g, cornering g)
- engineering tables (tire radius, ride frequency, race caliper hydraulics)

All values are class-typical figures for the archetype, rounded; no single real vehicle is reproduced.

## Inertia

Box approximation about the CG, scaled for mass concentration (`k < 1`: mass near the centre, e.g. mid-engine; `k → 1`: mass at the ends):

```
I_roll  = k_r · m·(W² + H²)/12
I_pitch = k_p · m·(L² + H²)/12
I_yaw   = k_y · m·(W² + L²)/12
```

| Axis | Box (kg·m²) | k | `inertia_kgm2` |
|---|---|---|---|
| roll | 600 | 0.78 | 470 |
| pitch | 2470 | 0.82 | 2030 |
| yaw | 2771 | 0.82 | 2270 |

## Aerodynamics

Frontal area A = 0.85·W·H = 2.06 m²; Cd = 0.45 → **CdA = 0.925 m²**. Lift Cl·A front/rear = -0.40 / -0.50 m² (class-typical; positive = lift). Add-on aero `aero_downforce_coeffs` = 0.40 F / 0.85 R m² (carbon front splitter with dive planes, flat floor with rear diffuser and a swan-neck rear wing at a medium-downforce endurance setting). Net downforce Cl·A 0.80 F / 1.35 R m² → 647 kg at 250 km/h, 37% front (static weight 48% front).

## Engine

5.5 L OHV 16-valve V8, naturally aspirated through two series air restrictors, dry sump, race calibration. Class-typical GT endurance V8 under its air restrictors (~425 kW at 7000 rpm, 660 N·m at 5000) per series homologation data; restrictors flatten the top end. Light flywheel and race cams: high idle, sharp throttle.

Peak **425 kW @ 7000 rpm**, **660 N·m @ 5000 rpm**. Idle 1500 / redline 7300 / limiter 7500 rpm. Rotating inertia 0.12 kg·m² (class: 0.10 small four … 0.30 big-block). Engine braking 12% of peak torque = 79 N·m. Power-to-weight 330 kW/t.

## Drivetrain

6-speed paddle-shift sequential rear transaxle (dog engagement, flat-shift ignition cut), plated rear LSD, carbon multi-plate clutch. Layout **RWD**; front diff: open; rear diff: clutch LSD, preload 120 N·m, power ramp 0.55, coast ramp 0.40. Clutch capacity 1.60 × peak torque = 1060 N·m. Shift time 0.15 s.

| Gear | Ratio | Overall | km/h @ redline |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2.90 | 9.92 | 97 |
| 2 | 2.07 | 7.08 | 135 |
| 3 | 1.62 | 5.54 | 173 |
| 4 | 1.32 | 4.51 | 212 |
| 5 | 1.11 | 3.80 | 252 |
| 6 | 0.96 | 3.28 | 292 |

Final drive 3.42, reverse 2.80. Speeds use the driven-wheel loaded radius 0.348 m.

## Suspension

Springs from ride frequency, `k = m_s·(2πf)²` with sprung corner mass `m_s = axle load/2 − unsprung`; dampers `c = 2ζ·√(k·m_s)`, ζ = 0.35 bump, rebound = 1.5 × bump.

| Axle | m_s | f | Wheel rate k | Bump c | Rebound c | Travel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Front | 285 kg | 2.60 Hz | 76100 N/m | 3260 N·s/m | 4890 N·s/m | 0.07 m |
| Rear | 309 kg | 2.80 Hz | 95600 N/m | 3800 N·s/m | 5700 N·s/m | 0.08 m |

Anti-roll bars from a roll-gradient target of 0.8°/g with 55% of roll stiffness at the front. Roll arm h − h_rc = 0.259 m (roll centres 0.08 m F / 0.12 m R). Required total K_φ = m·g·arm/φ = 234514 N·m/rad; springs give k·t²/2 = 109929 F / 134885 R N·m/rad; bars supply the rest as `arb_n_per_m = K_bar/t²` = **6600 F / 0 R N/m** (clamped at ≥ 0). Resulting gradient 0.7°/g, front share 49%. Bump stops 300000 N/m.

Alignment: camber -3.0° F / -2.0° R, toe -0.10° F / +0.15° R (+ = in), caster 7.0°.

## Brakes

Full-pedal line pressure 100 bar.

- Front: 380 mm disc, pistons per side 44 mm + 40 mm + 36 mm → A = 38.0 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 165 mm, pad μ = 0.52: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.52·100 bar·38.0 cm²·0.165 m = **6512 N·m**
- Rear: 355 mm disc, pistons per side 40 mm + 36 mm → A = 22.7 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 152 mm, pad μ = 0.5: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.5·100 bar·22.7 cm²·0.152 m = **3469 N·m**

ABS ceiling: caliper capacity 6512 / 3469 N·m exceeds 1.5 × the front lock torque on this car's tire (peak μ 1.36), which `wp_vehicle`'s ABS cannot modulate (it releases to a fraction of the commanded torque, so an oversized caliper keeps the wheel locked). Both axles scaled by 0.40 → **2620 / 1390 N·m**. Remove when 02's ABS modulates relative to lock torque.

Lock check at 1 g on μ = 1 (load transfer m·a·h/L): front needs 1282 N·m/wheel (capacity 2.04×), rear needs 851 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.63×).

`wp_vehicle` gives the axle `bias_front` favours its full `max_torque_*` and scales the other by (1 − b)/b, so `max_torque_*` holds the caliper capacity per wheel and `bias_front` acts as the proportioning valve: the rear is trimmed to the same lock margin as the front (ideal rear = T_f · lock_r/lock_f = 1738 N·m), never boosted above its caliper capacity. Rear capacity is below that (hardware-limited rear), so `bias_front` = **0.5**: both axles get full caliper torque → delivered 2620 N·m front / 1390 N·m rear per wheel at full pedal. Handbrake 1730 N·m per rear wheel.

## Steering

Ratio 11.5:1. Kerb-to-kerb turning circle 13.0 m → outer-front path radius 6.35 m, rear-axle-centre radius 4.89 m → mean road-wheel lock δ = atan(L/R) = **0.506 rad (29.0°)** (outer 25.3°, inner 33.9° at full Ackermann; `ackermann_frac` 0.30). Rack speed 2.2 rad/s.
